# Context recorded before checking

This is informed desired-source authoring for Issues #22, #27, #43 and #44,
not a controlled few-example model benchmark. Codex had already read the
adopted ordinary `T` / linear `Q<T>` direction, the 0.3.0 implementation plan,
the separate finite and sized ASTs and their current limitations. No external
model was invoked; the exact deployment and sampling settings are not recorded.

The ordinary-bit project isolates the adopted observation result `Bit` using
existing library operations. The unit project asks for a uniform zero-width
linear owner and ordinary singleton. The generic project is a desired grammar
experiment using Issue #33's still-proposed static brackets and #44's finite
basis parameter, with one algorithm body used at two distinct basis types.
Its existence does not adopt the proposed syntax or prove generic semantics.

Each complete source was saved and hashed before its first check. The baseline
is the unpublished 0.3.0-alpha worktree based on the commit in session.json,
including earlier review fixes and the adopted constitutional records. The
first command observations retain the actual selected executable hashes.
Contemporaneous native-contract proof work does not change executable checking
behavior. Rejection is an observed current limitation, not an invented failure
or a new constitutional obligation. Original files and outputs stay immutable;
later implementation checks must be appended separately.
